question: Which statement best describes Union types (A | B)?
options: To use a union safely you narrow it — use a runtime check that tells the compiler which member you have. typeof, instanceof, 'in', or comparing to a literal all narrow. Inside the checked branch, TypeScript treats the value as the specific member.

An intersection combines multiple types into one that has all their members simultaneously. A & B has every property of A and of B. It's most useful for merging object shapes — the result must satisfy every part at the same time.

A union type means a value can be any one of the listed types. string | number accepts a string or a number. You can only use members that are common to every member of the union until you narrow it, because TypeScript doesn't know which one you currently have.

Unions are most powerful with literal types: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' is a closed set of allowed values, far safer than string. The compiler rejects any value outside the set and gives autocomplete for the valid ones.
explanation: A union type means a value can be any one of the listed types. string | number accepts a string or a number. You can only use members that are common to every member of the union until you narrow it, because TypeScript doesn't know which one you currently have.
